findings.reachability_summary: internet → nginx-lb-01:443 (WAF) → app-server-01:8080 (IPS) (2 hops, WAF+IPS); office → nginx-lb-01:443 → app-server-01:8080 (2 hops)

reasons.claim: CVSS 10.0, network-exploitable with no privileges or user interaction (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N)
CVE is KEV-listed (added 2021-12-10) with EPSS 0.99999, so it is actively exploited in the wild
app-server-01 runs log4j-core 2.14.1, which falls in the vulnerable range >=2.13.0, <2.15.0
Asset is reachable from the internet and the office in 2 hops via nginx-lb-01:443 and app-server-01:8080, crossing ctrl-waf and ctrl-ips
Asset criticality is critical and it holds customer-pii, session-data and order-data. Computed priority is critical and always_review=true.
The Apache advisory lists fixed releases 2.3.1 (Java 6), 2.12.3 (Java 7) and 2.16.0 (Java 8 and later)

findings.mitigation_detail: Upgrade log4j-core on app-server-01 from 2.14.1 to 2.16.0 if it runs Java 8 or later (2.12.3 for Java 7, 2.3.1 for Java 6), per the Apache Logging Services advisory at https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/security.html. The matched_range from find_affected_assets is >=2.13.0, <2.15.0.
review_reasons: The find_affected_assets matched_range (<2.15.0) implies a fix at 2.15.0. The vendor advisory (chunk CVE-2021-44228_0_71) names 2.16.0, 2.12.3 and 2.3.1 as the fixed releases, and the CVE description says 2.15.0 is also affected. Please confirm the target version for the Java runtime in use.

findings.reachability_summary: internet → nginx-lb-01:443 (1 hop, WAF); office → nginx-lb-01:443 (1 hop, WAF)

reasons.claim: CVSS 7.5, network-exploitable with no authentication, availability-only impact (A:H)
Listed in KEV (added 2023-10-10) with EPSS 0.99999, so exploited in the wild
nginx 1.24.0 falls in the vulnerable range >=1.9.5, <=1.25.2
Reachable directly from the internet on port 443 in 1 hop, crossing only a WAF control
Priority is high: internet-reachable and unauthenticated, lowered one level because impact is DoS-only; asset criticality is high

The nginx maintainer states nginx is not considered affected in its default configuration, and recommends the limit_req directive as additional protection. This conflicts with the matched vulnerable range.

findings.mitigation_detail: Fixed version not stated in the available data (matched_range ends at the inclusive bound <=1.25.2); as a workaround, use the nginx "limit_req" directive to rate-limit and reject excessive requests (source: https://mailman.nginx.org/pipermail/nginx-devel/2023-October/S36Q5HBXR7CAIMPLLPRSSSYR4PCMWILK.html), and confirm the fixed release in the vendor advisory at https://lists.apache.org/thread/5py8h42mxfsn8l1wy6o41xwhsjlsd87q.
review_reasons: Conflicting evidence: find_affected_assets matches nginx 1.24.0 to the vulnerable range, but the nginx vendor advisory chunk (CVE-2023-44487_1_2) says nginx is not considered affected in its default configuration.
No fixed nginx version is stated in the tool results, so the exact remediation version needs confirming.

findings.reachability_summary: office-network → admin-host-01:22 (1 hop, no controls); not reachable from internet

reasons.claim: admin-host-01 runs openssh-server 9.3p1, within the vulnerable range >=8.6, <=9.8
CVSS 8.1 (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N), unauthenticated remote race condition in sshd; not in KEV
EPSS 0.995 (99.9th percentile), very high exploitation probability
Not reachable from internet; reachable from office network on port 22 in 1 hop with no controls crossed
Office-only exposure but asset holds sensitive data (ssh-private-keys, admin-audit-logs), criticality high, giving high priority
Vendor advisory says Portable OpenSSH 8.5p1 through 9.7p1 is affected and that the 9.8 release contains the fix

findings.mitigation_detail: Upgrade OpenSSH on admin-host-01 to the 9.8 release or a later one, which the vendor advisory at https://www.openssh.com/txt/release-9.8 says fixes this race condition, or install the distro's patched openssh package (e.g. RHSA-2024:4340).
review_reasons: The matched_range from find_affected_assets (>=8.6, <=9.8) includes 9.8 as vulnerable, but the vendor advisory says 9.8 contains the fix and that 8.5p1–9.7p1 is affected. The two sources conflict on the fixed boundary.
The installed version 9.3p1 may be a distro-backported build, so confirm the exact patched package version for this OS before closing the finding.

PostgreSQL PL/Perl environment variable changes execute arbitrary code
Incorrect control of environment variables in PostgreSQL
PL/Perl
allows an
unprivileged database user to change sensitive process environment variables
(e.g.
PATH
). That often suffices to enable arbitrary code execution, even if
the attacker lacks a database server operating system user. Versions before
PostgreSQL 17.1, 16.5, 15.9, 14.14, 13.17, and 12.21 are affected.
The PostgreSQL project thanks Coby Abrams for reporting this problem.
